never_started_tally.note: never_started holds the deep-read orders (fifteen a seat by metal cost, fourteen in seat 1); all_classified counts every order of the four seats (87) classified from frames.py's entry and the hands' lines; skipped are long walks that then started the same build and id partners whose id's frame stood (14)

mechanisms: The report lost the builder's own frame (seat 1 and seat 3, 893 metal): the hands end a builder's build task when any of our units of that type finishes within 250 of the task's site (crates/bot/src/brain/pianist/mod.rs, the Event::UnitFinished arm), so a neighbour's frame finishing made the entry read 'finishing an order' (or carry the neighbour's share) while the builder kept building, and the player stopped the 'stuck' builders: armadvsol_31825 (332), armadvsol_23138 (189), armllt_20968 (61); and in seat 3 the starter of coradvsol_18647 (311) was demoted to a repair-helper of its own frame by a watchdog refusal in the tick it created it, its entry said 'repairing our coradvsol' with no share, and re-lists dropped it because a repair is not a build in progress. Matching the task to the builder's own `created` frame (and keeping a repair-help frame in force across a re-list, or saying 'leaves the X at N%' in the queue result) keeps all four.

Turret frames started inside an enemy's reach while the metal store sat at 0, then shot down or left to the threat (seats 1 and 2, 835 metal): armhlt_28100 (383, left by the packet's Welder rule at 87% and shot down), armhlt_9506 (167), armbeamer_13042 (114, unseen artillery), armllt_18366 (78), armllt_2038 (68), armllt_11869 (25); each stood one to three minutes at store 0, so the threat arrived before the frame finished. The fix is the player's: fewer, covered turret frames at the front, or the metal concentrated on one at a time.

Metal starvation at the end (seat 2, 384 metal recoverable): armmoho_23112 stood 2:56 with its builder on it at metal store 0 (+14.5 to +19.5 a second over ten constructors and two labs, an energy stall 19:19-19:49) and ended at 62%; the at-end frames armllt_1998, armllt_20518 and armadvsol_14798 (204) stood under the same store. Smaller, by seam (54 metal): a stop or re-list written against a walking builder landed 10-31 s later, after the frame began (armllt_28016, armsolar_23869), and the old list's queued-ahead step stayed in the engine queue after a re-list and was started then dropped or duplicated (armllt_29241, armllt_13977, armllt_30891, coradvsol_21032).
